Graphic.description: One image file, or one page inside a multi-page container.

file.description: Image or container path. Omitted means "fall back to the resolved `scan.file`".

height.description: Pixel height of **this page**, not of the container.

mimetype.description: Explicit media type; otherwise inferred from the extension.

page.description: 1-based page index **inside** `file`. Omitted when `file` is a standalone image.

url.description: Direct download URL for this exact image (the retired `fetch` field).

width.description: Pixel width of **this page**, not of the container.

Holding.description: Where the physical object lives. Inherits, merged key by key.

collection.description: The named collection within the repository, e.g. `David Rumsey Map Collection`.

repository.description: Institution, e.g. `Bibliothèque cantonale et universitaire, Lausanne`.

shelfmark.description: Call number. **Always a string**, never an int — leading zeros and letters occur.

Link.description: Everything that is not the canonical `url`. Retires ad-hoc `index` and `fetch`.

Page.description: One scanned side, carrying graphics. **Declared inline only** — there is never a page file.

graphic.description:
Zero or more. Zero is legal (a text-only page) and emits `W904`.
The **first** entry is the primary graphic: the one `.pN` resolves to and the one
whose pixel space zone coordinates are in.

label.description:
The printed page label when it differs from `n`, e.g. roman `xxxvj`.
Purely descriptive: never parsed, never used for addressing.

n.description:
Page number **within its owning document**. This is what `.pN` matches.
Omitted means "continue the count". May be `0` (Turgot) or negative.

PageRange.description: A terse page range, `pages = { from = 13, to = 16 }`.

Resp.description: A statement of responsibility. Replaces the unparseable `author` string.

name.description: Person or corporate name as written.

role.description: One role or several. Both spellings are legal.

Rights.description: Rights status. Inherits, merged key by key.

attribution.description: Credit line, e.g. `Digitised by Google Books.`

scan.description: Rights status of the digitisation itself, distinct from the work.

work.description: Rights status of the intellectual work, e.g. `PD-old-100-expired`.

count.description: Number of pages in the container. Used by check 5. Does not inherit.

file.description:
Path to the container, relative to the directory of the file that **declared** it.
Inherits.

ppi.description:
Resolution the scan was made at, in pixels per inch. Inherits.

Stated rather than inferred: `render` otherwise has to guess a page's native
resolution from the largest image embedded in it.

url.description: Landing page for the digitisation, distinct from top-level `url`. Inherits.

Text.description: OCR or transcription. Never inline content.

by.description: Producing agent and version, e.g. `tesseract 5.3 fra`.

file.description: Path to the text file, resolved against the declaring file's directory.

Zone.description:
A rectangle on a page, in the pixel space of that page's **primary graphic**.

Zones are not addressable and not citable; nothing in the address grammar reaches them.

id.description: Page-local label. Not a global id, not addressable.

description: One TOML file in the primary source and scan archive. Generated from the Rust types in tools/src/model.rs by `scans schema` - do not edit by hand.

oneOf.description: The publication or work, independent of any copy.

covers.description:
EDTF interval. The span this source covers. Does not inherit.

This is where the legacy `held = "1789"` field lands.

date.description: EDTF. Date of the work, for single-work sources.

extent.description: Bibliographic collation, `"7 p. ; 18 cm."`. Does not inherit.

id.description: Stable flat id. Defaults to the filename stem.

of.description: Id of an ancestor. A source may be `of` another source (e.g. a series).

page.description: Legal on a source when copy and document are collapsed in (Turgot: 21 pages).

pages.description: Terse page range. Legal but unusual on a source.

resp.description:
Inherits wholesale. `Option` rather than a bare `Vec` because `resp = []` is the
documented way to *clear* an inherited value, and that must be distinguishable from
"not declared here".

scan.description: Legal on a source when the copy layer is collapsed in (Turgot, Verniquet).

subject.description: Subject headings as the cataloguer wrote them. Does not inherit.

url.description: Canonical landing page. Does not inherit.

oneOf.description:
One physical object that was digitised.

The inner type is named `CopyRecord` rather than `Copy` so it cannot be confused with
the `std::marker::Copy` trait in type position. The serde tag is taken from the
*variant* name, so the TOML still reads `layer = "copy"`.

covers.description: EDTF interval. The date span of material bound in this object. Used by check 6.

date.description: EDTF. Date of the object itself, if meaningful.

extent.description: Bibliographic collation, `"7 p. ; 18 cm."`. Does not inherit.

of.description: Id of the source (or another copy). Absent = orphan copy; legal, warns `W107`.

subject.description: Subject headings as the cataloguer wrote them. Does not inherit.

covers.description: EDTF interval, for documents spanning a range.

extent.description: Bibliographic collation, `"7 p. ; 18 cm."`. Does not inherit.

language.description: Inheritable scalar; present here so a document can override an ancestor's value.

of.description:
Id of **any** ancestor — copy, source, or another document.
Absent = standalone document (the one-off engraving case).

place.description: Inheritable scalar; present here so a document can override an ancestor's value.

subject.description: Subject headings as the cataloguer wrote them. Does not inherit.

title: Scan archive record
